newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan court bars testimony of ex-security chief.
newsitem.headline: Jordan court bars testimony of ex-security chief.

text.p: A Jordanian military court trying the killer of seven Israeli schoolgirls rejected on Thurday a defence plea to hear testimony of a veteran security figure chosen by King Hussein to investigate the shooting.

"Despite what the defence said that his excellency Muhammed Rasul al-Kailani has been authorised to undertake the investigation, this was a private assignment between him and His Majesty," Chief Judge Brigadier Mamoun al-Khasawneh heading the five-man military tribunal told the court.

King Hussein assigned Kailani, a veteran security chief who headed the powerful intelligence bureau in the 1960s and early 1970s, the task of directing the investigation into the causes behind the shooting by Private Ahmed Daqamsa at a border post in March.

Defence lawyer Hussein Majalli had earlier requested that the court hear Kailani's testimony as a key defence witness along with 25 others he read out including the soldier's family, his military superiors, comrades and independant medical doctors.
"Especially since His Majesty has said that he has assigned Kailani with the task of this investigation...it is the right of the court, with due respect to hear this witness," he said.
With the exception of Kailani, the court agreed to the list of defence witnesses whose testimony the court will begin to hear in the next session on Saturday.

Among the written evidence the defence submitted as part of their defence case on Thursday is a published message by King Hussein to this troops on March 20 in which he told them Daqamsa should have been shot dead on the spot.

Daqamsa's lawyers, opponents of Jordan's 1994 peace treaty with Israel who rallied to defend him as a hero, have argued before the trial started at the end of May that the king's comments prejudiced their client's chances of a fair trial.
Apart from the opening session of the trial, none of Daqamsa's large legal counsel have openly criticised the king for his comments.

Daqamsa has not denied shooting the girls, six of them 13 years old and one just 11 years old, but says he acted impulsively after being provoked during Moslem prayers. On Wednesday Daqamsa said he had no recollection of the shooting.
Daqamsa was stationed in Jordan's northern border territory of Baqoura, formally returned by Israel under the peace treaty but then leased back to Israeli farmers.
